units.text: Corrugated walls sweat in the heat.
A bare bulb swings from a cord, painting the cartons and a rolled carpet in slow, nauseous arcs.

Dust has settled on everything but the one thing that matters: a battered cassette recorder, its cover scarred with a boy's initials, sitting alone on an overturned milk crate as though somebody wanted it found.
A STRANGER, 40s, rain-dark coat, a crowbar hanging forgotten from his fist, stands over it.

He crouches, the knees of his trousers dampening on the concrete, and turns the machine over in his hands, and the lid pops, and a tape inside spins as he presses PLAY with a thumb that has not decided whether to tremble.
This is Desmond Archer, age eleven, and if you found this, Dad's lock didn't hold.
units.name: BOY'S VOICE

units.text: His breath catches, and in the pause between the tape's hiss and the next word, the bulb steadies, the carpet seems to exhale dust, and the crowbar slips from his hand and rings on the floor.
I put the key under the third brick. Take whatever's here. Just don't tell Mom.
units.name: BOY'S VOICE

units.text: He lifts a loose brick from the wall.
Beneath it: a small brass key, bright as the day it was hidden.
He closes his fist around it, rises, and walks out into the rain.
